gates.statement: a leader and a `deepdata replicate` follower stay agreed document for document across a leader restart, and a replica directory refuses both a second writer and a local write

A release gate rather than a MAC-01-style exemption, because unlike the darwin port this is a feature on the gated target -- Linux amd64 -- and the bar for a release should include what the release ships. Binds the three spike/multinode findings, which no package test can hold because each is about the space between two processes: a replica accepting a local write (split brain), post-restart writes never reaching the follower, and equal document counts hiding divergent contents. gates.statement: durable usage records survive restart
gates.note: DurableStore persists the usage tracker to a <basePath>.usage.json sidecar with each snapshot and on close, and reloads it at open (internal/collection/durable_store.go). Durability class B: an unreadable, corrupt or version-mismatched sidecar is logged and discarded whole, the tracker starts empty and the collection stays up with no fault latched; DurableStore.UsageLoaded reports the loss for a later status signal and is false only when a sidecar existed and was discarded. The check runs the internal/collection Usage tests plain and under -race.

gates.statement: darwin/arm64 binary survives boot, SIGKILL journal replay, and SIGTERM checkpoint cold start on real Apple hardware
gates.note: Not a release gate: Linux amd64 is the only gated release target, and widening what a release must pass is a separate decision from proving the darwin claim. The claim needs proving because store_lock_unix.go builds for `linux || darwin` and darwin binaries ship in bin/, while nothing has ever run one. The check writes its own schema-2 receipt to .deepdata-run/checks/darwin-durability/ instead of going through hardening_check.sh, which cannot run on macOS: BSD date has no -Iseconds, timeout is not installed, and its heredocs invoke `python`, which macOS does not ship. An empty finished_at from a half-written receipt fails gates.py's date regex and breaks `gates.py check` for the whole ledger, so a Mac receipt from hardening_check.sh would be worse than none. The check refuses to run off Darwin, because every assertion in it is platform-neutral and would pass on Linux without touching the port. Known Linux-only outside this check: soak.py and restart_reclaim_probe.py read /proc/<pid>/status VmRSS -- soak.py raises IndexError on the empty series and the reclaim probe silently returns -1 and reports a meaningless verdict; canonical_process_test.go:1131 asserts an exact os.ReadDir count that a .DS_Store breaks; and F_FULLFSYNC costs ~4.0ms/op against ~0.08ms on Linux, so per-document write loops may exceed Linux-tuned timeouts.

gates.statement: POST /docs/{id}/feedback stores feedback durably and is covered by tests
ephemeral collection class: documents write no journal record, the collection is empty after restart, /v3/status capabilities report the class
gates.note: ADR 0009 (accepted 2026-09-01). The ephemeral class is per collection: CollectionSchema.durability is "durable" (default when empty) or "ephemeral", and an ephemeral collection's insert/batch-insert/upsert/delete-doc apply under the store mutex but append no journal record, cost no fsync and do not advance AppliedLSN (DurableStore.appendApplyLocked), while snapshot v2 writes the collection with zero documents. Create-collection and delete-collection stay class A, so the collection's existence survives a restart and only its documents are lost; its upstream rebuilds them. Surface: durability on CollectionInfo, on the create and collections contract schemas, on CreateCollectionRequest/CollectionInfo in the proto (tag 6 each), on the Python TenantCollectionSchema/TenantCollectionInfo, and capabilities.durability_classes on GET /v3/status. Tests are internal/collection/ephemeral_test.go (no journal growth, empty after Close+reopen and after Checkpoint+reopen, unknown value rejected) and cmd/deepdata/ephemeral_test.go (HTTP round trip, status capabilities, gRPC mirror).
